title: Module Documentation: Turán's Hypergraph Problem (OPEN, $500 Prize)
content: The module docstring frames Problem #500 as one of the most famous open problems in extremal combinatorics. It states the central question: determine $\text{ex}_3(n, K_4^{(3)})$, the maximum number of 3-element subsets of an $n$-element set that avoid containing all four 3-subsets of any 4-element set. Turán's 1941 construction (3-partition) gives $(5/9 + o(1))\binom{n}{3}$ edges, Razborov's 2010 flag algebra bound gives $\leq 0.5612\binom{n}{3}$. Erdős considered this important enough to assign it Problem #500 with a \$500 prize. The problem remains completely open — the Turán density $\pi(K_4^{(3)})$ is unknown even to within a gap of $0.0056$.
mathContext: $\text{ex}_3(n, K_4^{(3)}) = \max\{|E| : E \subseteq \binom{[n]}{3},\; \forall S \in \binom{[n]}{4},\; \exists T \in \binom{S}{3},\; T \notin E\}$. Turán conjecture: $\lim_{n \to \infty} \text{ex}_3(n)/\binom{n}{3} = 5/9 \approx 0.5556$. Razborov 2010: $\leq 0.5612$. Gap: $0.0056$.

title: Imports and Setup: Combinatorics Infrastructure
content: Imports `Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic` (graph-theoretic context), `Mathlib.Data.Finset.Basic` (hyperedge collections as Finsets), `Mathlib.Data.Nat.Choose.Basic` (binomial coefficients $\binom{n}{3}$), and `Mathlib.Tactic` for proof automation. The section comment 'Core Definitions' marks the start of the four key predicates: `Hypergraph3`, `IsThreeUniform`, `ContainsK4_3`, and `IsK4Free`.
mathContext: The formalization represents 3-uniform hypergraphs as $\texttt{Finset}(\texttt{Finset}(\texttt{Fin}\ n))$ — a collection of subsets of the vertex set $[n]$. The $\texttt{Nat.choose}\ n\ 3 = \binom{n}{3}$ function counts the total number of 3-element subsets.

title: 3-Uniform Hypergraph Type
content: A 3-uniform hypergraph on vertex set $\texttt{Fin}\ n$ is a collection of 3-element subsets (edges). Unlike ordinary graphs (2-uniform), hyperedges connect triples of vertices. The type $\texttt{Hypergraph3}(n) = \texttt{Finset}(\texttt{Finset}(\texttt{Fin}\ n))$ allows arbitrary edge collections; 3-uniformity is enforced separately by $\texttt{IsThreeUniform}$. Using `Finset` of `Finset` (rather than `Multiset` or explicit `Fin 3 → Fin n`) ensures automatic deduplication of edges and vertex ordering.

title: 3-Uniformity Predicate
content: The predicate $\texttt{IsThreeUniform}$ requires every edge $e \in H$ to have exactly 3 vertices ($e.\text{card} = 3$). This is the higher-dimensional analogue of requiring all edges in a graph to be pairs. Requiring all hyperedges to have the same cardinality (k-uniformity) is the standard in hypergraph extremal theory, as it enables clean generalizations of graph-theoretic results.
mathContext: $\texttt{IsThreeUniform}(H) \iff \forall e \in H,\; |e| = 3$. $k$-uniform hypergraph generalizes: $\forall e \in H,\; |e| = k$.

title: $K_4^{(3)}$ Containment: The Forbidden Subhypergraph
content: $K_4^{(3)}$ is the complete 3-uniform hypergraph on 4 vertices, containing all $\binom{4}{3} = 4$ triples. `ContainsK4_3` formalizes containment: there exist 4 vertices $S$ (a Finset with `S.card = 4`) such that every 3-subset of $S$ is an edge of $H$. The $\exists S \wedge \forall T \subseteq S$ structure is the natural Lean encoding of 'contains $K_4^{(3)}$ as an induced subhypergraph'. This is the simplest forbidden subhypergraph whose Turán density is unknown — by contrast, $\text{ex}_k(n, K_r^{(k)})$ is known for all $r$ when $k = 2$ (graph Turán theorem).
mathContext: $\texttt{ContainsK4\_3}(H) \iff \exists S \subseteq V,\; |S| = 4 \wedge \forall T \in \binom{S}{3},\; T \in E(H)$. Note: $|K_4^{(3)}| = \binom{4}{3} = 4$ edges. For comparison, $K_r^{(2)}$ (graphs): Turán density $(r-2)/(r-1)$ [Turán 1941].

title: $K_4^{(3)}$-Free Hypergraph: The Central Predicate
content: A $K_4^{(3)}$-free hypergraph is 3-uniform and contains no 4 vertices spanning all 4 triples. Equivalently, every 4-vertex set misses at least one triple. `IsK4Free = IsThreeUniform ∧ ¬ContainsK4_3` is the conjunction of type constraint and forbidding condition. The Turán problem asks: what is $\max\{|E(H)| : \texttt{IsK4Free}(H)\}$ as a function of $n$? The remaining content in the file (lines 45-59) consists of comment stubs for the extremal number, density, bounds, and conjecture that would complete the formalization.
mathContext: $\texttt{IsK4Free}(H) \iff \texttt{IsThreeUniform}(H) \wedge \neg\texttt{ContainsK4\_3}(H)$. The Turán number $\text{ex}_3(n, K_4^{(3)}) = \max\{|E(H)| : \texttt{IsK4Free}(H) \text{ on } n \text{ vertices}\}$. Known: $(5/9)\binom{n}{3} \leq \text{ex}_3(n) \leq 0.5612\binom{n}{3}$ [Turán 1941, Razborov 2010].

title: Stubs: Extremal Number, Density, Bounds, and Conjecture (Incomplete)
content:
Lines 45-59 are section header comments and orphaned docstrings marking out the remaining formalization work:

**Turán number** (stub at line 45): `ex3_K4 n` would return the maximum number of edges in a $K_4^{(3)}$-free hypergraph on $n$ vertices, axiomatized with existence (`ex3_K4_achievable`) and optimality (`ex3_K4_optimal`) properties.

**Turán density** (stub at line 49): `turanDensityK4_3` would formalize $\pi(K_4^{(3)}) = \lim_{n\to\infty} \text{ex}_3(n)/\binom{n}{3}$, whose existence is guaranteed by the Katona–Nemetz–Simonovits theorem (1964).

**Turán's lower bound** (stub at line 50): $\pi \geq 5/9$ from the 3-partition construction.

**Razborov's upper bound** (stub at line 52): $\pi \leq 0.5612$ via flag algebras (2010).

**Turán's conjecture** (stub at line 54): $\pi = 5/9$ (OPEN since 1941).

**Exact small values** (stub at line 56): $\text{ex}_3(4) = 3$, $\text{ex}_3(5) = 7$, $\text{ex}_3(6) = 13$.
mathContext: Bounds hierarchy: $5/9 \leq \pi(K_4^{(3)}) \leq 0.5612$. Gap $\approx 0.0056$. Known exact values: $\text{ex}_3(4)=3$, $\text{ex}_3(5)=7$, $\text{ex}_3(6)=13$. Ratios: $0.75, 0.70, 0.65$ trending toward $5/9 \approx 0.556$. Formalizing these requires the flag algebra method — currently out of scope for Mathlib.
